nodes.summary: Let the men and the women form finite sets of the same size with complete strict preferences, and rank remaining single last for every agent. Then every stable matching with singles matches every man (and so, the sides having equal size, every woman). Hence, in the stable marriage problem, the rural hospitals theorem holds trivially.
nodes.title: With complete lists every stable matching is perfect

nodes.title: Stable matching with singles

nodes.summary: In a finite marriage market with singles, let `μ` and `ν` be stable matchings. A man who has a partner in `μ` has a partner in `ν`.
nodes.title: A man matched at one stable matching is matched at every stable matching

nodes.summary: Each man has a strict total order on `Option W`, where `none` is remaining single and `a` before `b` means that `a` is preferred (Roth, *Econometrica* 54 (1986), p. 425: a strict preference ordering over the set `H ∪ {u}`, with `u` the possibility of remaining unmatched).
nodes.title: Men's preferences with the option of remaining single

nodes.summary: In a finite marriage market with singles, a man has a partner at one stable matching if and only if he has a partner at every stable matching. With the men as Roth's students and every quota equal to one, this is the part of Roth's Lemma 1 saying that the set of students who are assigned positions is the same at every stable outcome.
nodes.title: Rural hospitals theorem, marriage case: every stable matching matches the same men

nodes.summary: In a finite marriage market with singles, a woman has a partner at one stable matching if and only if she has a partner at every stable matching. With the women in the role of Roth's hospitals and all quotas equal to one, this is Roth's Theorem: a hospital that fills fewer than its one position at a stable outcome, that is, a woman single at a stable matching, has the same (empty) assignment at every stable outcome.
nodes.title: Rural hospitals theorem, marriage case: every stable matching matches the same women

nodes.summary: For a strict preference `T` over partners, `withSingleLast T` is the strict preference over partners and the option of remaining single that agrees with `T` on partners and ranks remaining single below every partner. It describes an agent for whom every partner is acceptable, as in the complete preference lists of the stable marriage problem.
nodes.title: Remaining single ranked last

nodes.summary: A partial bijection `μ : M ≃. W` is stable for the men's preferences `mp` and the women's preferences `wp` if and only if its inverse `μ.symm : W ≃. M` is stable for the market in which the women propose the first coordinate, with preferences `wp` and `mp`. The definition of stability is symmetric in the two sides.
nodes.title: Stability does not depend on which side is called the men

nodes.summary: Let `mp` and `wp` be complete strict preferences, as in the stable marriage problem, and rank remaining single last for every agent. A perfect matching `μ : M ≃ W` is stable as a matching with singles, through `μ.toPEquiv`, if and only if it is stable in the sense of the stable marriage problem (no blocking pair). Individual rationality holds automatically, since every agent is matched to an acceptable partner.
nodes.title: Bridge to the stable marriage model

nodes.summary: Each woman has a strict total order on `Option M`, where `none` is remaining single (Roth, *Econometrica* 54 (1986), p. 426).
nodes.title: Women's preferences with the option of remaining single
